data: Last Soviet planetary mission; lost at Phobos approach
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

The last Soviet planetary mission. Reached Mars orbit in January 1989 but lost contact with Earth on March 27, 1989, just before its planned encounter with the moon Phobos. Phobos 2 returned 37 images of Phobos before contact was lost. The loss was attributed to an on-board computer failure causing loss of attitude control and power, though the complete sequence was never fully reconstructed.
Soviet companion orbiter to Mars 3 — orbited Mars from 1971-12-02 through 1972-08; first measurements of Mars upper atmosphere temperature
Soviet companion orbiter to Mars 2 — second spacecraft ever in Mars orbit (after Mariner 9 by 13 days). Operated 1971-11-27 to 1972-08
First spacecraft to orbit the Moon (or any body other than Earth) — entered lunar orbit 1966-04-03, three years before Apollo 8
First Jupiter orbiter; 8 years of measurements
First spacecraft to observe the Sun's poles from above + below the ecliptic — Jupiter gravity assist 1992
